football_evidence.question: Can North Dakota State contain New Mexico’s explosive runs?
football_evidence.assessment: Some measured evidence supports EdgeDesk’s lean toward New Mexico, and its own breakdown accounts for about 0.4 of the 2.8 points, but not the full gap. It is a research question, not a bet.
supporting: When New Mexico has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): New Mexico’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 10.1% of its runs, and North Dakota State’s defense stops 18.3% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.4%).

When North Dakota State has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): North Dakota State’s offense has allowed a sack on 4.6% of its dropbacks, and New Mexico’s defense sacks the quarterback on 8.7% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).

When North Dakota State has the ball (big plays on the ground): North Dakota State’s offense turns 6.0% of its runs into explosive gains, and New Mexico’s defense gives up explosive gains on 2.3% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.6%).

When North Dakota State has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): North Dakota State’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 15.5% of its runs, and New Mexico’s defense stops 24.6% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.4%).
contradicting: When New Mexico has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): New Mexico’s offense has allowed a sack on 11.7% of its dropbacks, and North Dakota State’s defense sacks the quarterback on 5.9% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).

When New Mexico has the ball (early downs): New Mexico’s offense succeeds on 39.0% of its first- and second-down plays, and North Dakota State’s defense allows success on 35.8% of first- and second-down plays (FBS average 42.7%).
In his last two games (Oklahoma and UTEP), Moga averaged 4.2 yards per attempt, against 7.3 in his two games before that.

When New Mexico has the ball (down-to-down efficiency): New Mexico’s offense succeeds on 41.2% of its offensive plays, and North Dakota State’s defense allows opponents to succeed on 36.1% of their plays (FBS average 42.4%).
quarterbacks: Toa Fa'avae has completed 41 of 74 passes (55.4%) for 698 yards, 9.4 yards per attempt, 5 touchdowns and 3 interceptions in six games for New Mexico, and has been sacked on 13 of 87 dropbacks.
Luke Moga has completed 23 of 39 passes (59.0%) for 248 yards, 6.4 yards per attempt, 3 touchdowns and no interceptions in four games for New Mexico, and has been sacked on 2 of 41 dropbacks.

Nathan Hayes has completed 106 of 163 passes (65.0%) for 1,272 yards, 7.8 yards per attempt, 10 touchdowns and 5 interceptions in seven games for North Dakota State, and has been sacked on 9 of 172 dropbacks.
